note: Replacement behaviors for Form TB-1: each one is a response the student is taught to use in place of a problem behavior, chosen to suit its function. Each entry was written for this workstation from the target and alternative-behavior definitions in the studies its note names (Journal of Applied Behavior Analysis and Behavior Analysis in Practice); nothing is quoted beyond a short phrase. The criteria follow the workstation's standard: 100% independent across 3 consecutive sessions for per-response measures; interval and time-sample measures keep their level. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and faded, with no physical guidance beyond what the student allows. Adapt each entry to the learner, the setting and the function shown by the assessment before teaching.

entries.lab: Asks for a break
entries.def: During a task, the student asks to stop for a short time in the planned form (says "break, please", signs BREAK, or hands or touches the break card) without problem behavior first, and goes to the break spot when the adult says yes.
entries.ex:
Hands the break card to the teacher after two math items and goes to the beanbag
Says "break, please" as the writing task is set down
Touches the BREAK button on the device while still seated (subtle)
Signs BREAK after finishing the step the plan requires
entries.nex:
Pushes the worksheet off the desk, then says "break" (problem behavior came first)
Leaves the table for the break area without asking
Says "break" only when the adult says "Say break" (prompted: recorded apart)
Asks for a snack during work (an item request)
entries.measure: Count each request; record independent and prompted requests apart, and the % of task opportunities with an independent request before any problem behavior.
entries.teach: Prompt the request as soon as the task is presented, before problem behavior can occur, and honor each request with a short break at first; then lengthen the work required before a break is given. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions, with no problem behavior before the request.
entries.note: Definition after Lalli, Casey and Kates (1995) and Johnson et al. (2004); the step-by-step prompting follows Hagopian et al. (1998). Problem behavior no longer produces the break while the request is taught.

entries.lab: Asks for help
entries.def: At a task step the student cannot yet do alone, the student asks for help in the planned form ("help, please", "I don't understand", a sign, or the help card) without a prompt and before problem behavior, then waits for the adult.
entries.ex:
Says "I don't understand" when a new kind of word problem appears
Raises the help card and waits at the desk
Says "help" quietly while looking at the adult, the pencil down (subtle)
Signs HELP when the zipper sticks
entries.nex:
Tears the worksheet, then asks for help
Says "help" right after the adult says "Say help"
Asks to stop the task (a break request)
Asks a peer for the answer during a test
entries.measure: Count each request at a hard step; independent and prompted apart; % of hard steps with an independent request before problem behavior.
entries.teach: Mix hard items with easy ones, prompt the request at the first hard item, and give real help each time; fade the prompt by delaying it a few seconds. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions at hard steps.
entries.note: Definition after Carr and Durand (1985) and Durand and Carr (1991). The help given must be real help with the step, not a break from it.

entries.lab: Asks for an adult's attention
entries.def: When the adult is busy, the student gets the adult's attention in the planned form (says the adult's name, taps the shoulder once, says "Am I doing good work?", or raises the attention card) without problem behavior first.
entries.ex:
Says the teacher's name and "look" in a normal voice during independent work
Raises the attention card above the head and waits
Taps the adult's shoulder once while the adult talks with another student (subtle)
Asks "Am I doing good work?" after finishing a row
entries.nex:
Screams, then says the adult's name
Taps the adult repeatedly until the adult turns
Calls out an answer during a lesson (calling out)
Asks for a toy (an item request)
entries.measure: Count each bid; independent and prompted apart; record the % of busy periods with an appropriate bid before any problem behavior.
entries.teach: Answer every appropriate bid at once at first and give problem behavior as little attention as safety allows; then show with a signal when the adult is free and when the student waits. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions, with no problem behavior before the bid.
entries.note: Definition after Carr and Durand (1985), Durand and Carr (1991) and Najdowski et al. (2008). Everyone answers the bid the same way.

entries.lab: Says "excuse me" and waits to be acknowledged
entries.def: When the student wants to speak to an adult who is talking with someone else, the student says "excuse me" once, then waits quietly, hands still, until the adult answers before going on.
entries.ex:
Says "excuse me", folds the hands and waits until the teacher turns
Stands beside the adult, says "excuse me" and waits 20 s without talking
Says "excuse me" softly and holds the question until the adult nods (subtle)
entries.nex:
Says "excuse me" and keeps talking over the adult
Repeats "excuse me" every few seconds
Pulls the adult's sleeve to be heard
Waits silently without ever asking (no request)
entries.measure: Count opportunities (the student wants an adult who is busy talking); score each as excuse me and wait, excuse me only, or interrupting; independent and prompted apart; latency from excuse me to acknowledgment.
entries.teach: Model the phrase and the wait in role-play, start with very short waits that the adult answers, then lengthen the wait as the student succeeds. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions, waiting up to the planned time.
entries.note: Definition after Hanley et al. (2014) and Ward et al. (2021).

entries.lab: Asks for an item or activity
entries.def: The student asks for a wanted item or activity in the planned form (a word or phrase such as "toys, please", a sign, a picture handed to the adult, or the device) instead of taking it or problem behavior.
entries.ex:
Says "iPad, please" when the tablet is on the shelf
Hands the picture of crackers to the adult
Says "May I have that, please?" to a peer holding the blocks
Points to the puzzle and says "puh" (an approximation the plan accepts) (subtle)
entries.nex:
Grabs the tablet from the shelf
Cries until the adult offers the item
Says the word only after the adult models it (prompted: recorded apart)
Names the item when the adult holds it up and asks "What is this?" (labeling, not a request)
entries.measure: Count each request; independent and prompted apart; % of opportunities (the item in view and wanted) with an independent request before problem behavior.
entries.teach: Start with the most likely form, prompt it as soon as the student shows interest, and give the item at once; fade the prompt with a short time delay. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Bourret, Vollmer and Rapp (2004), Najdowski et al. (2008) and Hagopian, Wilson and Wilder (2001).

entries.lab: Says or signs "all done"
entries.def: When the student wants an activity or item to end, the student says "all done", signs FINISHED, or uses the matching card or device button, before problem behavior and without leaving or throwing the materials.
entries.ex:
Signs FINISHED and pushes nothing away when the puzzle time is over
Says "all done" and hands the toy back
Taps the ALL DONE button on the device and sits back (subtle)
entries.nex:
Throws the toy, then says "all done"
Walks away from the table without signaling
Signs FINISHED only after the adult models it (prompted)
Says "all done" to mean the work is complete when it is not (checked against the task)
entries.measure: Count each signal; independent and prompted apart; % of opportunities with an independent signal before problem behavior.
entries.teach: Prompt the signal at the first sign of wanting to stop and end the activity at once at first; then ask for a little more before ending, step by step. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Groskreutz et al. (2014) and Falcomata et al. (2013).

entries.lab: Asks a person to stop
entries.def: When another person does something the student does not want (teasing, taking, crowding), the student says "stop" or "I don't like that" in a firm, ordinary voice, or signs STOP, and does not hit, push, or threaten.
entries.ex:
Says "Stop, I don't like that" when a peer pokes the student's arm
Signs STOP when a classmate keeps humming in the student's ear
Says "stop" and steps back when crowded at the cubbies (subtle)
entries.nex:
Shouts "stop" and pushes the peer
Says "stop" to an adult giving a task instruction (a break or "all done" request)
Says nothing and hits the peer
Repeats "stop" while chasing the peer
entries.measure: Count each provocation (simulated in practice, natural in class) and score: stop said without aggression, aggression, or no response; independent and prompted apart.
entries.teach: Teach in role-play with a familiar adult first, then a peer helper; adults answer the request by having the other person stop. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions in practice and in class.
entries.note: Definition after Fallon et al. (2025) and Groskreutz et al. (2014). When the other person goes on, the student walks away and tells an adult (Fallon et al., 2025).

entries.lab: Asks to play alone for a while
entries.def: When the student wants an interaction to end, the student asks in the planned form ("play by myself", "space, please", or the card), and the adult steps back for the planned time.
entries.ex:
Says "play by myself" while an adult comments on the student's drawing
Hands the "space" card to a peer who keeps talking
Turns slightly and says "alone, please" in a low voice (subtle)
entries.nex:
Pushes the adult away
Leaves the room to get away from a peer
Asks to stop a task (a break request)
Says "go away" with an insult
entries.measure: Count each request; independent and prompted apart; % of opportunities (an interaction the student is showing signs of wanting to end) with an independent request.
entries.teach: Prompt the request at the first sign that the interaction is unwanted and honor it at once; then lengthen the interaction a little before the request is honored. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Hagopian, Wilson and Wilder (2001).

entries.lab: Says "no, thank you" to an offer
entries.def: When offered something the student does not want (a food, an item, an activity choice), the student says "no, thank you", says "no", or shakes the head, and leaves the item without throwing or pushing it.
entries.ex:
Says "no, thank you" when offered carrots at snack
Shakes the head when offered the red crayon and points to the blue one
Says "no" quietly and slides the cup back a little (subtle)
entries.nex:
Throws the offered toy
Says "no" to a task instruction (noncompliance, a separate target)
Says "no" and screams
Pushes the plate off the table
entries.measure: Count offers of unwanted items; score a calm decline, problem behavior, or acceptance; independent and prompted apart.
entries.teach: Present preferred and nonpreferred offers mixed; prompt the decline on unwanted ones and honor it; keep instruction refusals out of these trials. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions with unwanted offers.
entries.note: Definition after Lalli, Casey and Kates (1995) and Neef, Walters and Egel (1984). A decline answers an offer; it is not a way out of required work.

entries.lab: Says "I don't know" to a question not known
entries.def: When asked a question the student cannot answer, the student says "I don't know" (or "I don't know, please tell me") instead of repeating the question or answering off topic, and answers questions the student knows.
entries.ex:
Asked "What is the capital of Peru?", says "I don't know"
Asked a new science question, says "I don't know, please tell me"
Asked "Where does milk come from?", shrugs and says "don't know" (subtle)
entries.nex:
Repeats "What is the capital?" (echoing)
Says "I don't know" to "What is your name?" (a known question)
Recites a video line instead of answering
Gives a wrong guess (scored as a wrong answer, not a target)
entries.measure: Probe known and unknown questions mixed; score "I don't know" to unknown questions, the correct answer to known ones, and echoes; % correct by question type.
entries.teach: Teach with a small set of unknown questions mixed with known ones and model the phrase; check that "I don't know" is not said to known questions. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions for unknown questions, with known questions answered.
entries.note: Definition after Schreibman and Carr (1978) and Ingvarsson et al. (2007).

entries.lab: Asks to go somewhere instead of leaving
entries.def: When the student wants to go to a place or an item beyond the area, the student asks in the planned form (words, a card, or a device), stays in the area, and waits for the adult's answer.
entries.ex:
Touches the "walk" card instead of running to the door
Says "Can I play with that door?" and points
Says "go outside?" at the classroom line and stays in line (subtle)
entries.nex:
Asks and runs at the same time
Leaves the area, then asks to go
Stands at the door without asking (approaching an exit, a precursor)
Asks for a break from work and stays seated (a break request)
entries.measure: Count each request; independent and prompted apart; record elopement on the same sheet and the % of opportunities with a request and no elopement.
entries.teach: Teach the request where elopement happens, honor it at once at first, then add short waits (see Waits for a requested item or activity). Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions, with no elopement.
entries.note: Definition after Piazza et al. (1997), Lehardy et al. (2013), Boyle et al. (2020) and Stevenson, Ghezzi and Valenton (2016). Any opening of an exit is also a safety event.

entries.lab: Waits for a requested item or activity
entries.def: After asking and hearing "wait" (or the wait card), the student says "okay" in an ordinary voice within 5 s and waits without problem behavior until the item, activity, or adult comes.
entries.ex:
Says "okay" and keeps playing with blocks until the tablet is ready 2 min later
Nods, says "okay" and sits with the wait card
Says "okay" with a small sigh and looks at the timer (subtle)
entries.nex:
Says "okay" and then grabs the item
Whines through the wait
Waits only because the adult is blocking the item (score the tolerance response only when it is the student's)
Leaves to find something else and does not come back (record as it happened)
entries.measure: Each wait is a trial: score the tolerance response within 5 s and a wait with no problem behavior; record the wait length; independent and prompted apart.
entries.teach: Begin with waits of a few seconds, model "okay", and let the wait end with the item; lengthen the wait in steps after successful waits. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently, for the planned wait length, in 100% of waits across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Ghaemmaghami, Hanley and Jessel (2016) and Hanley et al. (2014).

entries.lab: Accepts "no" or "not now"
entries.def: When a request is turned down or postponed, the student says "okay" in an ordinary voice (or nods), may take a slow breath as taught, and takes the offered alternative or moves on, without protest or problem behavior.
entries.ex:
Hears "not now, the computer is in use, but you can play catch", says "okay" and goes to play catch
Nods and puts the snack card back
Takes a slow breath, says "okay" and returns to the game (subtle)
entries.nex:
Says "okay" and keeps asking every few seconds
Argues "but you said"
Says "okay" while kicking the chair
Is not told no at all (the trial did not happen)
entries.measure: Each denial is a trial: score acceptance within 5 s with no problem behavior; independent and prompted apart; record the % of denials accepted.
entries.teach: Deny only some requests at first and offer an alternative with each denial; prompt "okay" at once and praise it; then deny more often, as the plan sets. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions (denials).
entries.note: Definition after Mace et al. (2011), Hanley et al. (2014) and Boyle et al. (2020).

entries.lab: Ends a preferred activity and hands over the item
entries.def: When told that the time with a preferred item or activity is over, the student stops within the planned time (for example 1 min) and hands over or turns off the item, without problem behavior.
entries.ex:
Turns off the video and hands the tablet to the parent within 1 min of the timer
Saves the game and gives the controller when told
Says "one more" once, then hands the tablet over in time (subtle: within the time)
entries.nex:
Hands it over after 5 min of pleading
Turns the screen away and keeps playing
Throws the tablet onto the couch
Hands over a different, unwanted item
entries.measure: Each ending is a trial: latency from the instruction to the hand-over; score within time without problem behavior; independent and prompted apart.
entries.teach: Give a warning before the end, praise and reward a prompt hand-over with access later or a token, and start with short, frequent practice endings. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions (endings), within the planned time.
entries.note: Definition after Wilder et al. (2007) and Hanley et al. (2014).

entries.lab: Moves to the next activity on the signal
entries.def: When the signal for the next activity is given (spoken, timer, or schedule card), the student stops the current activity and starts toward the next one within the planned time (for example 1 min), without problem behavior.
entries.ex:
Checks the schedule card and walks to the reading table when the timer ends
Lines up with the class at the bell within 30 s
Puts the blocks down with a frown and walks to the next center (subtle)
entries.nex:
Drops to the floor at the signal (dropping, a separate target)
Moves only after three repeated instructions
Starts toward the next activity and runs past it
Moves to the next activity before the signal
entries.measure: Each transition is a trial: latency from the signal; score on time without problem behavior; independent and prompted apart.
entries.teach: Show the next activity on a schedule, give a warning, and praise or reward prompt moves; shorten the warnings as the student succeeds. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions (transitions), within the planned time.
entries.note: Definition after Waters, Lerman and Hovanetz (2009) and Wilder et al. (2007). In Waters et al. (2009) the schedule alone did not lower problem behavior; adding extinction and differential reinforcement did.

entries.lab: Hands over an item when asked
entries.def: When an adult asks for an item that is not the student's or that must be put away, the student hands it to the adult within 10 s without problem behavior.
entries.ex:
Hands the peer's pencil case to the teacher when asked
Gives the scissors back at the end of art
Hands the item over slowly, looking at it, within 10 s (subtle)
entries.nex:
Drops the item on the floor near the adult
Hides the item in a pocket
Hands over a different item
Hands it over only after 30 s of bargaining
entries.measure: Each request for an item is a trial: latency to hand-over; score within 10 s; independent and prompted apart.
entries.teach: Pair asking with something the student likes (attention or a short trade) and practice with easy items first. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Donaldson, Trahan and Kahng (2014) and Wilder et al. (2007). Taking an item from the student by force is not part of this plan.

entries.lab: Does not touch a found firearm, leaves, and tells an adult
entries.def: On finding a firearm, the student does not touch it, leaves the area right away, and tells an adult within the planned time that a gun was found.
entries.ex:
Sees a gun on a shelf, backs out of the room and tells the teacher "there's a gun"
Leaves the closet and tells the parent within 10 s
Freezes, then walks out and says "gun" to the nearest adult (subtle)
entries.nex:
Picks up the gun to bring it to an adult
Leaves the room but tells no one
Calls a friend over to look
Touches it to check whether it is real
entries.measure: Score each probe on the 0 to 3 scale: 0 touched; 1 did not touch but did not leave or tell; 2 did not touch and left but did not tell; 3 did not touch, left, and told an adult.
entries.teach: Behavioral skills training: instruction, modeling, rehearsal and feedback, with practice in the real setting when rehearsal alone does not carry over. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: A score of 3 in 100% of probes across 3 consecutive sessions, with a follow-up probe later.
entries.note: Definition after Himle et al. (2004) and Vanselow and Hanley (2014). Probes use only a made-safe firearm, only with written consent, and are planned with the family and the school.

entries.lab: Does not touch medicine, poison or a lighter, leaves, and tells an adult
entries.def: On finding a listed hazard (medicine, a cleaning product, a lighter or matches), the student does not touch it, moves away within the planned time, and tells an adult what was found.
entries.ex:
Sees pills on the counter, leaves the kitchen and tells the parent "pills"
Walks away from a lighter on the bench and tells the teacher
Steps back from an open bottle under the sink and calls an adult (subtle)
entries.nex:
Picks up the bottle to hand it over
Leaves but does not tell
Opens the container to look
Tells an adult while still holding the lighter
entries.measure: Score each probe on a 0 to 3 scale: touched; did not touch but stayed; did not touch and left but did not tell; did not touch, left, and told.
entries.teach: Behavioral skills training with practice scenarios in the real rooms, with feedback after each probe. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: A score of 3 in 100% of probes across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Dancho, Thompson and Rhoades (2008), Petit-Frere and Miltenberger (2021) and Vanselow and Hanley (2014). Probe containers hold only harmless look-alike contents, with consent.

entries.lab: Asks an adult before eating or drinking anything found
entries.def: Before eating, drinking, or tasting anything not given by a known adult, the student asks a known adult first, or waits for one when none is there.
entries.ex:
Finds candy on a desk and asks "Can I eat this?"
Brings a found cup to the teacher and asks before drinking
Looks at a wrapped snack, puts it down and waits for the aide (subtle)
entries.nex:
Tastes it and then asks
Eats food from another student's lunch box
Asks a peer instead of an adult
Eats the snack the adult handed out (no question needed)
entries.measure: Score each probe with a planned, safe item: asked or waited, tasted, or ate; independent and prompted apart.
entries.teach: Teach the rule "ask a grown-up you know before eating or drinking anything" with modeling and rehearsal, then feedback in the real setting. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Asks or waits in 100% of probes across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Dancho, Thompson and Rhoades (2008). Probe items are safe foods or drinks chosen with the family.

entries.lab: Hands a found inedible item to an adult
entries.def: On finding an inedible item the plan lists (a cigarette butt, a small object), the student picks it up only to hand it to an adult, without bringing it to the mouth, and receives the planned trade.
entries.ex:
Hands a found cigarette butt to staff and gets the planned snack
Brings a bead from the floor to the teacher
Holds a found coin away from the face and walks it to the aide (subtle)
entries.nex:
Puts it to the lips, then hands it over
Pockets the item
Throws it away without telling
Hands over an item the adult had given
entries.measure: Score each found item (planted with planned, safe items, or natural): exchanged without mouthing, mouthed, or kept; % of items exchanged.
entries.teach: Plant safe target items, prompt the hand-over with a gesture, and trade each one for a preferred edible or item at first. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Exchanges with no mouthing attempt in 100% of items across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Goh, Iwata and Kahng (1999). Planted items must be safe if mouthed; the medical team sets the limits.

entries.lab: Says no, moves away, and tells an adult when lured by a stranger
entries.def: When an unknown adult invites the student to go along, the student says "no", moves away at least 6 m (or into a building) within the planned time, and tells a known adult.
entries.ex:
Says "no", walks to the school door and tells the teacher about the man in the car
Says "no" and runs to the parent at the park
Shakes the head, says "no" quietly, and goes to the aide (subtle)
entries.nex:
Agrees to go to see the puppy
Says "no" but stays talking
Leaves but tells no one
Says no to a known adult the family has named as safe
entries.measure: Score each planned probe on the 0 to 4 scale: 0 agrees to leave; 1 does not agree but does not say no, leave or tell; 2 says no only; 3 says no and leaves; 4 says no, leaves and tells.
entries.teach: Behavioral skills training with rehearsal of several lures, then practice in the real setting when needed. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: A score of 4 in 100% of probes across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Johnson et al. (2005) and Vanselow and Hanley (2014). Probes are arranged only with consent, with an adult the student does not know, and the student is told afterwards.

entries.lab: Stays within reach of the adult or the cart
entries.def: In the community, the student keeps one hand on the cart or stroller, takes the adult's offered hand by the student's own choice, or walks within arm's reach of the adult (the adult could reach the student with an extended hand), for the whole outing. Letting go of the adult's hand is allowed at any time and still counts while the student stays within reach.
entries.ex:
Keeps a hand on the shopping cart through the store
Takes the parent's offered hand to cross the parking lot, then lets go on the sidewalk and walks beside the parent
Drifts to the edge of reach and comes back without a prompt (subtle: still within reach)
entries.nex:
Walks two aisles ahead
Stays close only while an adult keeps hold of the student
Runs ahead and is called back (scored out of reach)
Rides in the cart seat (not scored: no walking)
entries.measure: Momentary time sample every 10 s (or each aisle or segment): within reach or not; % of samples within reach; prompts recorded.
entries.teach: Practice short outings with praise and small rewards for staying within reach, then lengthen the outings. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: In at least 90% of 10-s samples on each outing across 3 consecutive sessions (a time-sample measure keeps its level).
entries.note: Definition after Clark et al. (1977) and Piazza et al. (1997). The adult may offer a hand, but never takes hold of the student to keep the student close; the student chooses whether to take the hand, and where to put it. (The BCBA, 11/6: an offered hand, taken by the student's choice, counts.)

entries.lab: Stays with the group during walks and transitions
entries.def: On walks, in lines, and during transitions, the student stays with the group and within the planned distance of the adult (for example 1 m in one-to-one walking, or in the class line), from start to end.
entries.ex:
Walks in the class line from the classroom to the gym
Stays within 1 m of the aide on the walk to the bus
Steps out of line to look at a poster and steps back in within 2 s (subtle)
entries.nex:
Moves more than 1 m away from the adult
Runs ahead to the playground door
Stays near only when an adult walks between the student and the exit
Waits at the classroom (not part of the walk)
entries.measure: Duration or momentary time sample: % of the walk within the planned distance; count departures beyond it on the same sheet.
entries.teach: Rehearse the route, praise staying with the group often at first, and give the planned reward at the end of each walk; thin the praise as the walks go well. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Within the planned distance in at least 90% of the walk across 3 consecutive sessions (a duration measure keeps its level).
entries.note: Definition after Piazza et al. (1997) and Stevenson, Ghezzi and Valenton (2016).

entries.lab: Stops at the curb and waits for the signal
entries.def: At a curb or the edge of a road or parking lot, the student comes to a full stop on the curb, looks both ways, and waits for the adult's signal (or the walk light) before stepping off.
entries.ex:
Stops at the curb, looks left and right, and waits for the parent's "now"
Stops at the parking-lot edge and waits for the aide
Slows to a stop with the toes at the curb edge and looks both ways (subtle)
entries.nex:
Steps into the street, then stops
Stops but does not look
Crosses when the adult has not signaled
Stops at a curb with no road (a sidewalk step)
entries.measure: Each curb is a trial: score stop, look, and wait for the signal as steps of a task analysis; % of curbs with every step.
entries.teach: Teach at real curbs with the adult beside the student: instruction, modeling, practice and feedback at each crossing. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Every step at 100% of curbs across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Yeaton and Bailey (1978) and Yeaton and Bailey (1983). An adult always stays beside the student during practice.

entries.lab: Raises a hand and waits to be called on
entries.def: During group lessons, when the student has something to say, the student raises one hand to at least shoulder height and waits without calling out until called on; hands stay down when there is nothing to say.
entries.ex:
Raises one hand during a question and waits to be called
Keeps the hand up quietly while another student answers
Lifts the hand to shoulder level and lowers it when the question is answered (subtle)
entries.nex:
Raises the hand while calling out "me, me"
Raises both hands and waves them
Raises the hand to every question without an answer
Gets up and walks to the teacher
entries.measure: Each question to the group is an opportunity: score hand raised and waited, call-out, or no response; record the accuracy of raises (hand up only when the student has an answer).
entries.teach: Practice in small groups with a secret word or a held item, praising correct raises and correct hands down; then move to the class. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions (raised only when the student has something to say).
entries.note: Definition after Charania et al. (2010) and Chan and O'Reilly (2008).

entries.lab: Makes on-topic comments
entries.def: In conversation, the student makes comments related to the current topic, and when wanting to change the topic says so first ("Can we talk about something else?").
entries.ex:
During talk about the weekend, says "I went to the park too"
Asks the peer a question about the peer's drawing
Says "Can I tell you about my game now?" before switching (subtle)
entries.nex:
Brings up the same favorite topic again
Corrects the peer's way of playing (lecturing)
Answers with a video line
Switches topic with no lead-in
entries.measure: Count on-topic comments and off-topic or restricted-topic comments per conversation; % of comments on topic.
entries.teach: Give attention (an interested answer) to on-topic comments and brief, neutral responses to off-topic ones; practice with a familiar peer. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: On topic in 100% of comments in planned conversations across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Roantree and Kennedy (2012) and Hagopian, Kuhn and Strother (2009).

entries.lab: Talks about the current activity
entries.def: The student makes statements that fit the setting and the current activity (about the work, the people present, plans for the day), instead of statements the team has listed as delusional or out of place.
entries.ex:
Says "I finished counting the combs" during a work task
Comments "the bus is late today" at the bus stop
Asks "What is next?" during a lull (subtle)
entries.nex:
Repeats a listed unusual belief
Makes a sexual remark about a classmate (a separate target)
Recites a script unrelated to the task
Is silent (no statement to score)
entries.measure: Count contextual and listed statements per session; rate per hour of each, or % of statements contextual.
entries.teach: Give prompt, warm attention to contextual statements and little attention to the listed ones; agree the listed statements with the mental-health provider. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Contextual in 100% of statements in planned sessions across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Travis and Sturmey (2010). Listed statements are reviewed with the mental-health provider before and during the plan.

entries.lab: Reports own actions honestly
entries.def: When asked about something the student did (for example, "Did you touch the tablet?"), the student says clearly what was done, including a broken rule.
entries.ex:
Says "yes, I played with it" after touching a forbidden toy
Tells the teacher "I took the eraser"
Nods and says "I did" quietly (subtle)
entries.nex:
Says "no" after doing it
Blames a peer
Says "maybe" or changes the subject
Says "no" when the student truly did not do it (an honest "no", also correct)
entries.measure: Each question about a known act is a trial: score honest or not; record the act itself apart; % of honest reports.
entries.teach: Reinforce honest reports generously and do not punish what was reported in the same moment; teach in planned practice first. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Honest in 100% of questions across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Lehardy et al. (2023). Honesty is taught first, then the broken rule is addressed (Lehardy et al., 2023).

entries.lab: Asks to join play
entries.def: When the student wants to play with peers, the student asks ("Can I play?", "Do you want to play?") and waits for an answer, then joins or chooses another activity.
entries.ex:
Asks "Can I play?" at the edge of the block area and waits
Invites a peer "Want to play tag?"
Sits beside the group and says "me too?" (subtle)
entries.nex:
Takes a piece from the game to join it
Jumps into the game without asking
Asks and then grabs the toy when told "not now"
Follows the peer who has said no
entries.measure: Count requests and invitations; score the request and the student's response to a yes or a no; independent and prompted apart.
entries.teach: Teach with role-play and a peer helper, then prompt at the start of free play and fade the prompt. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions when wanting to join.
entries.note: Definition after Kohler and Fowler (1985) and Hanley et al. (2014).

entries.lab: Asks for a turn and waits for it
entries.def: When a peer has the item, the student asks for a turn ("May I have that, please?", "My turn next?") and waits until the item is offered, without taking it.
entries.ex:
Says "May I have the red car, please?" and waits
Asks "Can I go next?" at the swing and waits in line
Shows an open palm and says "turn?" without touching the item (subtle)
entries.nex:
Asks and grabs at once
Takes the item when the peer looks away
Says "It's mine" (claiming, a precursor)
Waits silently for a long time without asking (no request)
entries.measure: Each opportunity (a wanted item held by another): score request and wait, request only, or taking; independent and prompted apart.
entries.teach: Practice with an adult and then a peer, giving the turn quickly at first and lengthening the wait. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Najdowski et al. (2008) and Hanley et al. (2014).

entries.lab: Greets with words, a wave or a handshake
entries.def: When meeting someone, the student greets in a planned, socially fitting form (says "hi" with the person's name, waves, or offers a handshake or high five), at a comfortable distance.
entries.ex:
Says "Hi, coach" and waves when the coach comes in
Stands up and offers a handshake to a visitor
Gives a high five to a classmate who raises a hand for one
Smiles and lifts a hand briefly (subtle)
entries.nex:
Hugs a visitor without asking
Touches a peer's face to say hello
Shouts the greeting from across the room repeatedly
Waves at nobody in particular (not a greeting)
entries.measure: Each arrival or meeting is an opportunity: score a planned greeting, touching without permission, or none; % with a planned greeting.
entries.teach: Model and practice greetings with familiar adults, use a short written or picture prompt, then fade it. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions (arrivals and meetings).
entries.note: Definition after Hood, Luczynski and Mitteer (2017) and Hagopian, Kuhn and Strother (2009).

entries.lab: Asks before touching or hugging
entries.def: Before touching or hugging someone, the student asks ("Can I have a hug?", "High five?") and touches only after a yes, and only in the ways the plan allows.
entries.ex:
Asks "Can I hug you?" and waits for the parent's yes
Asks a peer "High five?" and gives one after the peer raises a hand
Stops a step away and asks "hug?" (subtle)
entries.nex:
Hugs first, then asks
Asks and touches before the answer
Asks a stranger for a hug
Touches a private area (a separate safeguarding target, never this entry)
entries.measure: Count touches with and without asking; % of touches preceded by a request and a yes.
entries.teach: Practice with familiar adults, praise asking, and offer a planned alternative (a high five) when the answer is no. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions before touching.
entries.note: Definition after Hagopian, Kuhn and Strother (2009). Touch of private areas is a safeguarding matter and is never replaced by this entry alone.

entries.lab: Works on the assigned task (on task)
entries.def: The student is oriented to the assigned materials, the teacher, or the speaking classmate, and does what the task asks (writing, reading, answering when asked).
entries.ex:
Writes answers on the worksheet
Looks at the teacher during the lesson and answers when called
Reads the page, pausing to think with eyes on the book (subtle)
entries.nex:
Draws on the desk during writing time
Looks around the room
Talks with a peer about the weekend
Sits with the pencil but no writing for the whole interval
entries.measure: 10-s momentary time sample or whole interval during work periods; % of intervals on task; record the work completed beside it.
entries.teach: Praise on-task work often and give little attention to off-task behavior; break work into short parts at first. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: In at least 80% of 10-s intervals across 3 consecutive sessions (an interval measure keeps its level).
entries.note: Definition after Hall, Lund and Jackson (1968) and Hardesty, Lerman and Hardee (2023).

entries.lab: Follows an instruction within 10 s
entries.def: After an adult gives an instruction, the student begins the response within 10 s and completes it.
entries.ex:
Starts putting away the books within 5 s of "clean up"
Turns off the video within 10 s when asked
Begins slowly within 10 s and finishes (subtle)
entries.nex:
Begins after 30 s
Says "okay" and does not start
Starts and stops halfway
Starts before the instruction
entries.measure: Each instruction is a trial: score compliance (start within 10 s and completion); % of instructions followed; independent and prompted apart.
entries.teach: Give a few easy instructions the student usually follows before a harder one, praise compliance at once, and give clear, single instructions. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions (instructions).
entries.note: Definition after Mace et al. (1988) and Wilder et al. (2007).

entries.lab: Asks to go to the calm space
entries.def: When upset or early in an escalation, the student asks in the planned form ("calm space, please" or the card) to go to the agreed calm space, goes there, and returns when the planned time or the timer ends.
entries.ex:
Hands the calm-space card to the teacher and goes to the quiet corner
Says "I need the calm space" when a peer is loud
Points to the calm-space picture while clenching the hands, then walks there (subtle)
entries.nex:
Runs out of the room to calm down
Goes to the calm space and stays for the rest of the day
Is sent to the calm space by the adult (not a request)
Asks for the calm space to avoid every task (record; review the plan)
entries.measure: Count each request; independent and prompted apart; time to return; record whether problem behavior came before the request.
entries.teach: Show the calm space when the student is calm, practice going there and back, and prompt the request at the first precursor. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions when a precursor occurs, with return on time.
entries.note: Definition after Hagopian, Wilson and Wilder (2001) and Lalli, Casey and Kates (1995), adapted to a calm space the student chooses to use. The calm space is never a locked or seclusion room.

entries.lab: Takes slow breaths as taught
entries.def: When told "not now", when upset, or at the planned cue, the student takes the slow breaths as taught (for example, in through the nose and out through the mouth, two or three times) and then says "okay" or goes on with the plan.
entries.ex:
Breathes in and out slowly twice and says "okay" when the computer is not available
Stops, takes a breath and walks away when a peer teases
Takes one slower breath with the shoulders dropping before answering (subtle)
entries.nex:
Breathes fast and shallow
Holds the breath
Breathes slowly while shouting
Breathes slowly at rest with no cue (not scored)
entries.measure: Each cue is a trial: score the taught breathing within 5 s; independent and prompted apart.
entries.teach: Model and practice the breaths when calm, then prompt them at planned denials or cues, with praise. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Independently in 100% of opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions (cues).
entries.note: Definition after Boyle et al. (2020) and Fallon et al. (2025). Breathing is taught as a skill the student uses, never as a demand when the student is in crisis.

entries.lab: Uses a fidget or hand item as planned
entries.def: The student manipulates the planned item (a squeeze ball, a fidget, a textured toy) with the hands, at the desk or in the lap, while continuing the activity, and does not throw it or use it to disturb others.
entries.ex:
Squeezes the stress ball under the desk while listening
Turns the textured toy in the hands during story time
Presses the pin toy with the thumb now and then (subtle)
entries.nex:
Throws the ball to a peer
Bangs the fidget on the desk
Plays with the fidget instead of writing for the whole work period
Mouths the item (record as mouthing)
entries.measure: Momentary time sample: item in use as planned, target behavior, or neither; % of intervals with the target behavior beside the % with the item in use.
entries.teach: Choose items by a competing-stimulus assessment, offer them freely at first, and agree when and where they are used. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Target behavior in at most the level the plan sets, with the item used as planned in 100% of the work periods across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Breeman et al. (2025) and Goh et al. (1995). Items are chosen by assessment, not by guess, and are checked for safety.

entries.lab: Uses the taught competing response at the urge
entries.def: When the student notices the urge or the first movement of the habit, the student does the taught competing response (for example, folds the arms or presses the hands flat on the desk or thighs) for 1 min, or the planned time.
entries.ex:
Folds the arms for 1 min when the hand rises toward the hair
Presses the hands flat on the desk for 1 min at the urge to bite the nails
Stops the hand halfway to the face and rests it flat on the thigh (subtle)
entries.nex:
Finishes the pull, then folds the arms
Holds the response for 5 s only
Uses the response with no urge, all day (record; review the plan)
Covers the hair with a hat (an environmental change, not the response)
entries.measure: Count competing responses and their duration (self-record or observer); count the habit beside it; % of urges or onsets followed by the response.
entries.teach: Awareness training first (describing and noticing each occurrence), then rehearsing the response, with praise from the people who support the student. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: The response at 100% of noticed urges, held for the planned time, across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Woods, Miltenberger and Lumley (1996), Rapp et al. (1998) and Twohig and Woods (2001). In Twohig and Woods (2001), 1- and 3-min responses kept their effect; 5 s did not.

entries.lab: Records own behavior on a self-monitoring sheet
entries.def: At each cue (a vibrating timer or the end of an interval), the student marks on the sheet whether the planned behavior happened, and the mark agrees with the adult's record.
entries.ex:
Checks "yes" for working when the timer vibrates
Marks a tally for each hand raise
Marks "no" honestly after a stereotypy episode (subtle: an honest mark counts)
entries.nex:
Marks "yes" for every interval without looking
Forgets to mark at the cue
The adult marks for the student
Marks long after the cue
entries.measure: Count cues with a mark; % of marks that agree with the adult's record; the target behavior is recorded on its own sheet.
entries.teach: Teach the sheet and the cue with practice and feedback, reward accurate marking, then fade the adult's checking. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Marks at 100% of cues, agreeing with the adult in 100% of them, across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Stahmer and Schreibman (1992) and Woods, Miltenberger and Lumley (1996).

entries.lab: Accepts a bite
entries.def: When a bite is presented, the student opens the mouth and lets the whole bite in (or brings it in by self-feeding) within 5 s, without turning away or pushing the spoon.
entries.ex:
Opens the mouth within 3 s and takes the spoonful of yogurt
Picks up the cracker and bites it within 5 s
Opens a little, then wider, and takes the bite at 4 s (subtle)
entries.nex:
Opens after 10 s
Takes only part of the bite on the lips
Turns the head and then accepts after a second presentation (score the second one)
Accepts a preferred food offered between trials (not a trial)
entries.measure: Each presentation is a trial: score acceptance within 5 s; % of bites accepted; record expulsions and packing apart.
entries.teach: Present small bites of foods the feeding team has cleared, praise and reward each acceptance, and increase bite size or new foods in steps. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Within 5 s in 100% of presentations across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Ahearn et al. (1996), Patel et al. (2002) and Ewry and Fryling (2016). A feeding plan is set with the medical and feeding team; escape extinction is their decision, not this entry's.

entries.lab: Swallows the bite (mouth clean)
entries.def: Thirty seconds after accepting a bite, no food or liquid is visible in the student's mouth, and none was expelled.
entries.ex:
Shows an empty mouth at the 30-s check
Swallows and opens the mouth to show
Swallows in two goes and the mouth is empty at the 30-s check (subtle)
entries.nex:
Food held in the cheek at 30 s (packing)
Spits the bite into a napkin
Clean only after 2 min
No bite was accepted (no trial)
entries.measure: Each accepted bite: check at 30 s; % of accepted bites with mouth clean.
entries.teach: Reinforce mouth clean at once, adjust texture with the feeding team when packing persists, and keep bites small. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Mouth clean in 100% of accepted bites across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Patel et al. (2002). Texture and swallowing safety are set by the feeding team.

entries.lab: Walks heel to toe
entries.def: Each step the student takes lands with both the heel and the front of the foot touching the ground.
entries.ex:
Walks down the hall with heel-to-toe steps
Heel touches first on each step across the gym
One step lands toe-first and the next ones heel first (subtle: score each step)
entries.nex:
Walks on the toes
Heel touches only when standing still
Runs on the toes during PE (score only walking, as planned)
Jumps (not walking)
entries.measure: 10-s partial interval of walking (an interval with any toe step is scored toe walking), or each step counted; % of intervals with heel-to-toe walking only.
entries.teach: Feedback from heel squeakers or praise for heel-to-toe steps, with small rewards at first; ask the physical therapist first. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: In at least 90% of 10-s intervals of walking across 3 consecutive sessions (an interval measure keeps its level).
entries.note: Definition after Wilder et al. (2020). Toe walking is reviewed by a physician or physical therapist before a behavioral plan.

entries.lab: Uses the toilet and asks to go
entries.def: The student urinates or has a bowel movement in the toilet, and asks to use the restroom (in the student's own way of communicating) or walks there without a prompt between scheduled trips.
entries.ex:
Asks "bathroom" with the device and voids in the toilet
Voids in the toilet at a scheduled sit
Walks to the restroom door on the student's own (subtle: a self-initiation)
entries.nex:
Wet underwear at a dry check
Sits but does not void (not an appropriate void; record the sit)
Goes only when prompted (prompted: recorded apart)
Voids outside the toilet
entries.measure: Record each void: in the toilet or an accident; % of voids in the toilet; count self-initiations apart.
entries.teach: A dense sitting schedule with reinforcement for voids in the toilet, then thinning the schedule and teaching the request; medical review first. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Voids in the toilet in 100% of voids across 3 consecutive sessions, with self-initiations.
entries.note: Definition after Perez et al. (2020) and Perez et al. (2021). Bowel and bladder concerns go to the medical provider first.

entries.lab: Uses the bedtime pass and stays in bed
entries.def: After goodnight, the student stays in bed, or uses the bedtime pass for one short trip out (a drink, the toilet, one more hug) and returns to bed, without calling out.
entries.ex:
Hands the pass to the parent for a drink and goes back to bed
Stays in bed all night with the pass unused
Calls out once, quietly, then stays in bed (subtle: record the call)
entries.nex:
Leaves the room without the pass
Uses the pass and then calls out again
Stays up playing in the room
Comes out after the pass has been used
entries.measure: Parent log each night: calls and exits after goodnight, pass use; nights with no call or exit beyond the pass.
entries.teach: Give the pass at goodnight, explain it simply, and answer only the pass; review the log weekly with the family. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: No calls or exits beyond the pass on 100% of nights across 3 consecutive weeks.
entries.note: Definition after Freeman (2006). A sleep or health concern is reviewed with the family and the medical provider.

entries.lab: Stays calm and still during dental or medical care
entries.def: During each step of a dental, medical, or grooming procedure, the student keeps the head and body still and quiet (no crying, moaning, or pushing away), and may use the taught signal to ask for a planned short rest.
entries.ex:
Keeps the mouth open and still for the count of 10
Lies still for the ear check and raises a hand once for a pause
Whimpers once, then stays still (subtle: score the interval)
entries.nex:
Turns the head away at each step
Pushes the instrument away
Is kept still by an adult (not cooperation; never part of this plan)
Is asleep or sedated (not scored)
entries.measure: 15-s intervals during each step: cooperative or disruptive; % of intervals cooperative; count rest signals.
entries.teach: Practice each step before the visit, give short rests and praise for cooperation, and build the time a little each visit. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Cooperative in at least 90% of 15-s intervals across 3 consecutive visits or practice sessions (an interval measure keeps its level).
entries.note: Definition after Allen and Stokes (1987). Brief rests were earned by cooperation in that study; the team agrees the signal with the dental or medical provider.

entries.lab: Uses the matched-stimulation items
entries.def: The student engages with the items chosen to give stimulation like that of the target behavior (for example, a light-up toy for visual stereotypy, music for vocal stereotypy) in the way the item is used.
entries.ex:
Watches and turns the light-up spinner during free time
Listens to music with headphones instead of humming loudly
Holds a vibrating toy against the palm during a wait (subtle)
entries.nex:
Holds the item without using it
Uses the item as part of the target behavior (banging it)
Engages with an unmatched item (record which)
Is prompted through use the whole time (prompted)
entries.measure: Momentary time sample: engaged with a matched item, target behavior, or neither; % of intervals of each.
entries.teach: Identify matched items by assessment, give free access at first, and then use them in the planned periods. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Target behavior at the level the plan sets with engagement in at least 80% of 10-s intervals across 3 consecutive sessions (an interval measure keeps its level).
entries.note: Definition after Piazza et al. (2000) and Piazza et al. (1998).

entries.lab: Chews or mouths the planned oral item
entries.def: The student mouths or chews only the planned oral item (a chew tool or a food the feeding team has cleared), instead of non-food items, clothing, or the hand.
entries.ex:
Chews the chew tube during circle time
Eats the cleared crunchy snack from the pouch when the urge comes
Rests the chew tool between the teeth during reading (subtle)
entries.nex:
Mouths a pencil
Chews the shirt collar
Drops the chew tool and puts a toy in the mouth
Bites the hand
entries.measure: Momentary time sample or count: planned item in the mouth, target behavior, or neither; % of intervals; count pica attempts apart.
entries.teach: Find the preferred texture by assessment, keep the item within reach, and prompt a switch to it at the first sign of mouthing. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: Target behavior at the level the plan sets with the planned item in use in 100% of mouthing episodes across 3 consecutive sessions.
entries.note: Definition after Piazza et al. (1998) and Piazza et al. (2000). Chew items and foods are cleared by the feeding team for choking risk.

entries.lab: Plays with toys or leisure items as designed
entries.def: The student uses toys or leisure materials in the way they are made to be used (building with blocks, rolling a car, drawing), with or without an adult nearby.
entries.ex:
Builds a tower with blocks
Rolls the car along the track
Colors in the book, looking now and then at a peer (subtle)
entries.nex:
Spins the car wheels and watches them
Lines the blocks up and fixes the line
Throws the toys
Looks at a forbidden tablet while holding a toy
entries.measure: 10-s intervals: appropriate play, target behavior, or neither; % of intervals with appropriate play.
entries.teach: Teach play actions with modeling and praise, then self-management or a short schedule so play continues without an adult. Prompts are spoken, shown or modeled and then faded; no physical guidance beyond what the student allows.
entries.crit: In at least 80% of 10-s intervals of free time across 3 consecutive sessions (an interval measure keeps its level).
entries.note: Definition after Stahmer and Schreibman (1992) and Lehardy et al. (2023).
